Subject: Post-call technical recap & next steps — SDK / auth / JSON reliability

Hi Nora / Michael,

Thanks again for taking the time today — appreciate the clear rundown of the DataForge constraints and the throughput targets. Below is a concise technical recap from our side plus proposed next steps so we can align on the workshop scope.

Recap (what we heard)
- Peak concurrent requests: ~120 RPS across two regions (US east primary, EU for backups)
- Hard latency target: 95th <= 300ms for short completions (<= 64 tokens)
- Need structured outputs for enrichment pipeline (strict JSON schema, minimal human parsing)
- Plan to use embeddings for semantic search + a reranker for top-K reordering
- Preference for hosted API for POC; potential Private deployment for production compliance later

Key technical proposals
1) SDK + Auth
   - Provide language-specific quickstart SDKs (JS/Python) that include a one-shot auth helper.
   - Recommend API key for initial POC, OAuth2 (client credentials) for production + rotating keys via KMS.
   - SDK will surface helper to attach idempotency key and request metadata (region, model_hint, route).

2) Routing & availability
   - Route requests by region -> model family -> fallback model. Canary policy for new model variants.
   - Support a cost/latency tier flag in SDK to prefer smaller quantized models when under load.

3) Structured output reliability (the bit we discussed at length)
   - Primary approach: Constrained decoding + JSON schema validation pipeline:
     a) Prompt with constrained-output template + schema hint (few-shot examples)
     b) Use token-level constraints where possible to bias generation toward schema tokens (e.g., enumerations)
     c) Server-side validator: run fast JSON parse + schema validator; if invalid, apply deterministic sanitizer (strip trailing commas, fix quotes) and revalidate
     d) If still invalid, automatic retry with alternative decoding parameters (increase temperature=0.0? reduce sampling) and limit retries to 2 attempts to preserve latency SLOs
   - Provide client-side validator in SDK to fail-fast before sending into your pipeline and to optionally accept relaxed parsing.

4) Embeddings & reranker integration
   - We recommend storing both dense embeddings + source metadata for re-ranking. Redwood will return embeddings in the same call or via batched endpoint.
   - Reranker should be model-driven (scoring top-N retrieved candidates). Keep reranker model as smaller, dedicated ranker to save cost.

Action items / proposed next steps
- Schedule a 60m joint tech workshop (eng + infra) — we'll bring Marcus and Laura for deep-dive (SDK, auth flow, and schema validation code samples).
- I'll attach a short tech playbook + sample schema and arch diagram for your review (attached).
- Please share any compliance constraints (e.g., on-prem requirement, encryption-only-of-payload) ahead of session.

Available slots: Tue 5/4 09:00–11:00 PT, Wed 5/5 13:00–16:00 PT, Fri 5/7 10:00–12:00 PT.

Thanks — attaching a short playbook and a sample JSON schema to review.

Best,
Dylan Brooks

Redwood Inference

Dylan — thanks for the tidy recap, looks like you captured our constraints well. A couple quick clarifications before the workshop: 

1) Latency: our 95th <= 300ms target is end-to-end (including embed + reranker) for the short path. If you can show a viable pattern that keeps the text-generation path sub-200ms, that would be helpful.
2) Retries: we absolutely need idempotency & dedup to avoid double-charging or duplicate writes; can you confirm how the SDK will expose idempotency keys and how the platform guarantees at-most-once semantics for side-effecting requests?
3) Embeddings: are embeddings returned synchronously in the same request or do you recommend a batched embedding job for larger datasets? We might want synchronous small batches during search.

We prefer Tue 5/4 09:30 PT for the workshop. Also: we will likely bring our security lead (Michael) and one infra engineer.

On compliance: DataForge will need audit logs for all inference requests and the ability to purge PII on request — we'll send a list of requirements to you separately.

Appreciate it — Nora

Subject: Internal: DataForge — tech playbook notes (SDK/auth/routing/schema)

Dylan / Laura — following up with some concrete engineering notes I want us to bring to the workshop. Copying short checklist and sample code references.

SDK & Auth- Quickstart libs: node (fetch wrapper) + python (requests/asyncio) with examples for both API key and OAuth2 client-credentials.- Idempotency: SDK will accept a request-id header (Idempotency-Key). Server stores short TTL for those keys (~24h) and returns HTTP 409 if replay with different body; for side-effects we recommend idempotency + at-least-once handlers on your side, but we can also offer at-most-once for supported flows (requires idempotency audit).

Routing logic- Client can pass region preference; server chooses closest available zone.
- Model hint + fallback order (e.g., rwd-extend-2b -> rwd-extend-7b-quant -> rwd-embed-compact) with canary percentage routing.

Structured output reliability- Two-stage validation pattern we recommend:
   1) Constrained generation stage: include schema + canonical examples in prompt; use token-biasing for critical tokens (open-source support varies by backend).
   2) Deterministic post-processing: run a lightweight JSON parse + ajv-like schema validator; if parse fails, run a sanitizer that: fixes trailing commas, normalizes smart quotes, ensures top-level braces.
   3) Retry policy: up to 2 automated retries server-side with different decoding params (greedy/beam, strict decoding flags), then escalate to a textual fallback payload with an explicit \"parsing_hint\" flag so your pipeline can surface manual review.

Edge cases + fallback- If the downstream pipeline cannot accept non-JSON, provide a wrapped envelope: {"ok": false, "error_type": "invalid_json", "raw": "<model output>"} so you can audit.

Embeddings + reranker- Allow synchronous small-batch embeddings (<=128 items) for search latency targets.
- Reranker: run ranking model on top-N (N=20) candidates; include scores and explainability tokens in the response.

Attachments (for session)
- sample-output-schema.json (simple order/fields example)
- arch diagram: shows SDK -> proxy -> model pool -> validator -> reranker -> store

I'll upload a short playbook and code snippets to the shared drive. Putting together a short demo that shows invalid JSON -> automated sanitization -> successful retry.

— Marcus
